messages.subject: Memory Issues
parts:
I've run into an issue with NIMBLE running out of memory on my machine, and I was hoping there might be some strategies to reduce memory use.  

I've emailed (wouldn't let me attach a document that large) my .RData file with the necessary elements and I'm using the nimbleMCMC() call.  I've tried simply asking for summary and not samples.  I also wondered if not reporting WAIC would help; however, ideally I'd like to get the WAIC out.




Mod.2.0.8<-nimbleCode({
  for(p in 1:P){
    
    
    
    for(g in 1:G){
      
      q.raw[p,g] ~ dgamma(shape=alpha[p,g], scale=1)  #ALPHA VALUES TOO SMALL FOR GAMMA TO SAMPLE
      q[p,g] <- q.raw[p,g] / sum(q.raw[p,]) 
      
      cutoff[p,g]<-max(q.raw[p,])
      
      z.mat[p,g]<-step(q.raw[p,g] - cutoff[p,g] + .0001)
      
      
      alpha[p,g] ~ dgamma(shape=10,scale=10)
      
    }
    
  }
  
  
  for(p in 1:P){
    
    w.s[p] ~ dbeta(shape1=1,shape2=1)
    w[p] <- w.s[p] / w.sum
    
  }
  
  w.sum<-sum(w.s[])
  
  
  
  for(p in 1:P){
    
    for(g in 1:G){
      w.mat2[p,g]<- w[p]*z.mat[p,g]
    }
  } 
  
  
  for(i in 1:I){
    for(j in 1:J){
      for(g in 1:G){
        
        grp.term[i,j,g]<-phi[g]*beta[g]*(pols.std[i,j,1]*w.mat2[1,g] +
          pols.std[i,j,2]*w.mat2[2,g] +
          pols.std[i,j,3]*w.mat2[3,g] +
          pols.std[i,j,4]*w.mat2[4,g] +
          pols.std[i,j,5]*w.mat2[5,g] +
          pols.std[i,j,6]*w.mat2[6,g] +
          pols.std[i,j,7]*w.mat2[7,g] +
          pols.std[i,j,8]*w.mat2[8,g])
        
      }
    }
  } 
  
  for(i in 1:I){
    for (j in 1:J){                    
      y[i,j] ~ dpois (lambda=mu[i,j])     
      
      log(mu[i,j]) <- a0 +
        grp.term[i,j,1] +
        grp.term[i,j,2] +
        grp.term[i,j,3] +
        grp.term[i,j,4] +
        grp.term[i,j,5] +
        grp.term[i,j,6] +
        grp.term[i,j,7] +
        grp.term[i,j,8] +
        eps[i] + 
        
        e[i] +
        
        gamma[j]
  
      
      
      
    }
  }
  
  
  gamma[1] ~ dnorm(0, sd=sd.gamma)
  
  for(j in 2:J){
    gamma[j] ~ dnorm(gamma[j-1],sd=sd.gamma)
  }
  
  for(i in 1:I){
    e[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd=sd.e)
    
  }
  
  for(k in 1:numNeigh){
    weights[k]<-1
  }
  
  eps[1:I] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:numNeigh], weights[1:numNeigh], num[1:I], tau.eps, zero_mean = 1)
  
  for(g in 1:G){
    phi[g] ~ dbinom(size=1, prob=rho[g])
    rho[g] ~ dbeta(shape1=1,shape2=1)
    
    
    beta[g] ~ dnorm(0, sd=sd[g])
    #tau[g]<-pow(sd[g], -2)
    sd[g] ~ dunif(min=0.01,max=5)
  }
  
  
  #tau.e<-pow(sd.e,-2)
  sd.e ~ dunif(min=0.01,max=5)
  
  tau.eps ~ dgamma(2, 0.5)
  sd.gamma ~ dunif(min=0.01, max=10)
  a0 ~ dnorm(0, sd=sd0)
  #tau0<-pow(sd0,-2)
  sd0 ~ dunif(min=0.01,max=5)
  
  
})



  mysim <- nimbleMCMC(code = Mod.2.0.8, constants = nimble.constants,
                      monitors=c( 'z.mat','q'),
                      data = nimble.data, inits = nimble.inits,
                      nchains = 1, niter = 15000, nburnin = 10000, thin=5,progressBar = T,
                      summary = TRUE, WAIC = T, samples = F)

Hi Ray,

It turned out that you stumbled into a model-specific problem in the configureMCMC step that was accidentally introduced in a relatively recent release.  This is not what I expected to find.

I've pushed a fix to our devel branch.  You can install by

library(devtools)
install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble")

Thanks for your patience on this one.

I think you'll find it faster to work outside of nimbleMCMC to save some steps that you don't need:

m <- nimbleModel(Mod.2.0.8, constants = nimble.constants, data = nimble.data, inits = nimble.inits, 
                 calculate = FALSE) ## calculate=FALSE is faster

conf <- configureMCMC(m, useConjugacy = FALSE) ## useConjugacy = FALSE is faster, if you don't need Gibbs (conjugate) sampling

Then use buildMCMC and runMCMC.

We're working towards releasing version 0.8.0 soon.  I think that will have efficiency improvements to configureMCMC, but you will have to turn them on via a nimbleOption to try them.  We'll make it clear in release notes.

-Perry

      q[p,g] <- q.raw[p,g] / sum(q.raw[p,]) 
      
      cutoff[p,g]<-max(q.raw[p,])
      
      z.mat[p,g]<-step(q.raw[p,g] - cutoff[p,g] + .0001)
      
      
      alpha[p,g] ~ dgamma(shape=10,scale=10)
      
    }

  for(p in 1:P){
    
    w.s[p] ~ dbeta(shape1=1,shape2=1)
    w[p] <- w.s[p] / w.sum
    
  }
  
  w.sum<-sum(w.s[])
  
  
  
  for(p in 1:P){
    
    for(g in 1:G){
      w.mat2[p,g]<- w[p]*z.mat[p,g]
    }
  } 
  
  
  for(i in 1:I){
    for(j in 1:J){
      for(g in 1:G){
        
        grp.term[i,j,g]<-phi[g]*beta[g]*(pols.std[i,j,1]*w.mat2[1,g] +

          pols.std[i,j,8]*w.mat2[8,g])

    }
  } 
  
  for(i in 1:I){
    for (j in 1:J){                    
      y[i,j] ~ dpois (lambda=mu[i,j])     
      
      log(mu[i,j]) <- a0 +
        grp.term[i,j,1] +
        grp.term[i,j,2] +
        grp.term[i,j,3] +
        grp.term[i,j,4] +
        grp.term[i,j,5] +
        grp.term[i,j,6] +
        grp.term[i,j,7] +
        grp.term[i,j,8] +
        eps[i] + 
        
        e[i] +
        
        gamma[j]
  
      
      
      
    }
  }
  
  
  gamma[1] ~ dnorm(0, sd=sd.gamma)
  
  for(j in 2:J){
    gamma[j] ~ dnorm(gamma[j-1],sd=sd.gamma)
  }
  
  for(i in 1:I){
    e[i] ~ dnorm(0, sd=sd.e)
    
  }
  
  for(k in 1:numNeigh){
    weights[k]<-1
  }
  
  eps[1:I] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:numNeigh], weights[1:numNeigh], num[1:I], tau.eps, zero_mean = 1)
  
  for(g in 1:G){
    phi[g] ~ dbinom(size=1, prob=rho[g])
    rho[g] ~ dbeta(shape1=1,shape2=1)
    
    
    beta[g] ~ dnorm(0, sd=sd[g])
    #tau[g]<-pow(sd[g], -2)
    sd[g] ~ dunif(min=0.01,max=5)
  }
  
  
  #tau.e<-pow(sd.e,-2)
  sd.e ~ dunif(min=0.01,max=5)
  
  tau.eps ~ dgamma(2, 0.5)
  sd.gamma ~ dunif(min=0.01, max=10)
  a0 ~ dnorm(0, sd=sd0)
  #tau0<-pow(sd0,-2)
  sd0 ~ dunif(min=0.01,max=5)
  
  
})

parts: A clarification:  The fix to the problem you encountered will definitely be in 0.8.0.  *Other* efficiency improvements will be available by turning on an option.  They will go in a future release after they've been tested more thoroughly.

On Wed, May 29, 2019 at 3:00 PM Perry de Valpine <pdeva...@berkeley.edu> wrote:
Hi Ray,

It turned out that you stumbled into a model-specific problem in the configureMCMC step that was accidentally introduced in a relatively recent release.  This is not what I expected to find.

I've pushed a fix to our devel branch.  You can install by

library(devtools)
install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble")

Thanks for your patience on this one.

I think you'll find it faster to work outside of nimbleMCMC to save some steps that you don't need:

m <- nimbleModel(Mod.2.0.8, constants = nimble.constants, data = nimble.data, inits = nimble.inits, 
                 calculate = FALSE) ## calculate=FALSE is faster

conf <- configureMCMC(m, useConjugacy = FALSE) ## useConjugacy = FALSE is faster, if you don't need Gibbs (conjugate) sampling

Then use buildMCMC and runMCMC.

We're working towards releasing version 0.8.0 soon.  I think that will have efficiency improvements to configureMCMC, but you will have to turn them on via a nimbleOption to try them.  We'll make it clear in release notes.

-Perry
